notes: Ask Leo answers your questions itself: it sees the board, reads a card in full and searches the web. It only adds cards or starts an agent when you ask.
Agents can read the board and add or change cards, for example one card per thing they find.
Chatting with an agent on a card updates the card: it shows the agent working, then the result.
When a request drops before any answer shows, OpenLeo sends it again.
A computer that stops responding restarts on its own, so the agent's screen no longer stays on "Connecting".
Site icons look right for more sites.
In the Mac app, a sideways swipe over a list scrolls the board, and ⌘R reloads.
The chat stays where you are while an agent works, and only jumps down when you send a message.
The first release built from the public repository. The app itself is the same as 0.10.9.
The first desktop release, for Mac (Apple silicon), Windows and Linux.

Setup walks you through giving your agents a computer, with Apple's container tool on new Macs or Docker everywhere else. It downloads the computer ready-made for your chip, and on Windows it can switch Docker to the Linux containers it needs.

OpenLeo updates itself. It looks for a new version when it opens and every few hours, gets it ready in the background, then offers a restart. You can also choose Check for Updates… in the OpenLeo menu or the menu bar icon.
The Mac app is signed and checked by Apple, so it opens without the "unidentified developer" warning.
Open on your other devices: use OpenLeo from your phone or laptop, wherever you are, through Tailscale. Turn it on from your account menu and scan the code. See the guide.
